narrative:
The model estimates a 44% chance that you will leave your current role. Because this probability is high enough to flag risk, the organization has decided to deny your promotion.

The decision was driven primarily by three aspects of your profile. First, the number of training programs you attended in the past three years had the strongest influence, but in a positive direction: having completed seven or more programs actually pulled the prediction toward staying. This is notably higher participation than the 33% of employees predicted to stay who attended none.

Two experience-related factors worked against you and ultimately outweighed the training benefit. Your six-to-ten years of total professional experience and your one-to-five years in the current organization both pushed the model toward predicting you would leave. While these experience levels are fairly common among employees the model expects to stay (roughly one-third have 6–10 years overall and half have 1–5 years here), the combination signaled higher turnover risk to the model.

The organization should review whether your extensive recent training is being fully utilized in your current role and discuss clearer growth paths that match your experience. You may want to explore how your skills could be better leveraged internally or what opportunities exist elsewhere that better align with your career stage.
